1	# Benchmark Datasets
2	
3	> Datasets and runner plumbing exist and have been exercised offline; no
4	> outcome-improvement or savings claim is established (see
5	> [Evaluation Framework](EVALUATION.md)).
6	
7	This document defines the benchmark dataset format (`evaluation/dataset.ts`
8	validates it; `evaluation/runner.mjs` runs it) and how paired baseline-versus-
9	governed comparisons are produced and read.
10	
11	## Scope
12	
13	- **Dataset**: small, versioned, reproducible workload documents under
14	  `benchmarks/` (schemaVersion `"1"`). Each workload specifies a task, bounded
15	  context inputs, a starting state (`setup`), a scripted reference solution
16	  (`solution`), and objective completion/test checks (`checks`).
17	- **Offline and credential-free**: fixture contents are inline in the JSON,
18	  test invocations are argv arrays restricted to `node`, and no network or
19	  external service is contacted.
20	- **Isolation**: workspaces materialize under the OS temp directory
21	  (`runner.mjs` uses `os.tmpdir()`), never in the repository checkout, so runs
22	  cannot alter the working tree. Baseline and governed runs get separate fresh
23	  workspaces.
24	
25	## Workload document
26	
27	One JSON file per workload; subdirectories group categories
28	(`benchmarks/coding/…` today). Unknown fields are rejected rather than ignored.
29	
30	```json
31	{
32	  "schemaVersion": "1",
33	  "id": "issue-fix-boundary",
34	  "category": "coding/issue-fix",
35	  "task": "Fix src/b

1	# Context Classifier
2	
3	> Experimental and deliberately narrow. It classifies from explicit metadata
4	> only; it does not inspect content, use an LLM, or contact any external
5	> service. Classification is a convenience in front of the existing inventory
6	> ingestion contract, not a replacement for callers supplying a type.
7	
8	The classifier is the Phase 1 deliverable behind `src/classify/classify.ts`
9	(contracts in `src/types/classifier.ts`, tested in `tests/classifier.test.ts`).
10	It answers one question — "what context type should this item carry?" — from
11	explicit signals, and refuses to answer when the signals do not support one.
12	
13	## Inputs and signals
14	
15	`classifyContext` takes a `ContextClassificationInput`:
16	
17	- `explicitType` (optional) — caller-provided type. When present it always
18	  wins: it is honoured even if it is an extension outside the known vocabulary
19	  (`knownType: false` records that), and conflicting signals never rewrite it.
20	- `source` (required) — normalized: trimmed, lowercased, hyphens folded to
21	  underscores, then split on whitespace/commas/semicolons into tokens.
22	- `tags` (optional) — normalized to trim + lowercase + hyphen fold; tags match
23	  the vocabulary by exact text, they are not token-split.
24	
25	Content is never inspected: the classifier cannot and does not guess from
26	content. Anything not in the signal vocabulary matches nothing.
27

$ git commit <<'EOF'
fix: bound benchmark spawn environment, surface read errors, fold tag hyphens

Benchmark test children now run with the parent environment replaced (empty
env) and the interpreter pinned to process.execPath, so dataset scripts can
never inherit credentials. The runner and docs replace the old "offline and
credential-free" claim with the honest trust boundary: dataset test scripts
execute arbitrary trusted code, and no filesystem/network isolation is
claimed because no stable cross-platform sandbox exists on supported Node
versions (24+).

Completion checks now distinguish a genuinely missing path (ENOENT, the only
"absent" result) from other read failures: an existing directory or an
unreadable entry surfaces as UnexpectedWorkspaceReadError instead of
passing a file_absent check or silently failing a file_contains check.

Tag normalization in the classifier now folds hyphens to underscores as
documented, so a "git-diff" tag classifies as diff while tags stay exact-
match; regression tests cover the credential-free spawn, ENOENT versus
directories, and hyphenated tags.
EOF
